title: Email & Username Investigation
description: Learn how to investigate email addresses and usernames as starting points for building a target's public digital footprint. Covers verification, GHunt, BSSID, and username enumeration.

sections.title: Email as a Starting Point
sections.description: An email address is not a direct path to a person's identity. It is a starting point for further investigation. The email may contain a username or identifier that appears on other publicly accessible services.
topics: Email may never have been publicly indexed by search engines
Website containing it may block search-engine indexing
Could belong to an organization, business, or public figure
Email username part may appear on other platforms
Always verify the email first before deeper investigation
sections.note: Never treat email investigation as: Find email → Find person. Think of it as a starting point. Verify first, then investigate step by step.

sections.title: Email Verification Tools
sections.description: These tools help verify whether an email address is valid and discover publicly associated information.

tools.name: EmailSherlock
tools.description: Search for publicly associated information using an email address or username. Verify email existence and find linked accounts.

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.description: Search for publicly available contacts and information associated with an organization or domain. Pre-installed in Kali Linux.

tools.name: Hunter.io
tools.description: Find and verify professional email addresses by company domain. 25 free searches per month.

tools.name: Epieos
tools.description: OSINT tool for email investigation. Finds Google account info, social profiles, and breach data linked to an email.

commands.description: Search for emails and subdomains associated with a company domain using Google.
Search all available sources for emails, hosts, and IPs related to a domain.
Search LinkedIn specifically for employees and emails of a company.

sections.title: GHunt — Gmail OSINT
sections.description: GHunt is an OSINT tool that gathers publicly available information associated with Google accounts and Gmail addresses. It can reveal account details, linked services, and more.
sections.note: GHunt can only work with information that is publicly available. Not every Gmail address will return the same amount of information.

tools.name: GHunt
tools.description: OSINT tool for Gmail and Google account investigation. Requires authentication setup via GHunt Companion Firefox extension.

Install GHunt dependencies. Use a Python virtual environment (venv) for cleaner setup.

Start GHunt authentication. Select Option 2, then use GHunt Companion Firefox extension to get the Base64 code.
Investigate a Gmail address. Returns publicly available account info, linked services, and more.
Investigate a Google account using its Gaia ID (internal Google account identifier).
Investigate a publicly shared Google Drive file or folder URL.

sections.title: BSSID Investigation
sections.description: BSSID (Basic Service Set Identifier) is the MAC address of a wireless access point. Location databases sometimes associate BSSIDs with approximate geographic locations collected over time.
sections.note: A BSSID is NOT an exact location and does NOT directly reveal GPS coordinates. Treat any location returned as an approximate lead that needs independent verification.

commands.description: Look up approximate location associated with a Wi-Fi access point BSSID using GHunt.
Free BSSID geolocation API. Returns approximate lat/long associated with a Wi-Fi access point.
Example BSSID lookup via terminal. Replace MAC address with target BSSID.

sections.title: Username Investigation Tools
sections.description: Username investigation helps discover where a specific username appears across the internet. Always manually verify results — a matching username does not mean all accounts belong to the same person.
sections.note: Automated tools can produce false positives. Compare profile pictures, bios, linked websites, posting patterns, and other independent indicators before making any attribution.

tools.name: Sherlock
tools.description: Search for a username across 300+ platforms. Open-source Python tool.

tools.name: WhatsMyName
tools.description: Username enumeration across hundreds of sites. More accurate than Sherlock for some platforms.

tools.name: Namechk
tools.description: Check username availability across social networks and domains. Useful for finding registered accounts.

tools.name: UserSearch.org
tools.description: Search for a username across multiple social platforms simultaneously.

sections.title: Metadata Extraction — Hidden Data in Files
sections.description: Every file — image, PDF, Word document — contains hidden metadata. This can reveal the author's name, GPS coordinates, device info, software used, and creation timestamps. Most people never think about this.
sections.note: Images shared on social media often have GPS stripped by the platform. But images shared via direct links, forums, or personal websites may still contain full EXIF data.

tools.name: ExifTool
tools.description: Most powerful metadata extraction tool. Works on images, PDFs, videos, audio, and 100+ file formats.

tools.name: Jeffrey's Exif Viewer
tools.description: Online EXIF viewer. Paste any image URL to extract metadata without downloading.

commands.description: Extract all metadata from an image. May reveal GPS, device model, software, timestamps.

Export metadata from all JPG files to a CSV for analysis.

sections.title: Certificate Transparency Logs
sections.description: Every SSL/TLS certificate issued for a domain is publicly logged. This reveals ALL subdomains — including internal, staging, and forgotten ones that never appear in search engines.
sections.note: This is one of the most underused OSINT techniques. Companies often expose internal infrastructure through certificate logs without realizing it.

tools.name: crt.sh
tools.description: Free certificate transparency search. Find all subdomains and certificates for any domain.

tools.name: Censys
tools.description: Search engine for internet-connected devices and certificates.

commands.description: Find ALL subdomains of target.com via certificate transparency logs. The % is a wildcard.
Get certificate data as JSON and format it for easy reading.

commands.cmd: curl -s 'https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com&output=json' | python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(d['name_value']) for d in json.load(sys.stdin)]" | sort -u
commands.description: Extract and deduplicate all subdomains from certificate transparency logs.
Search certificates registered with a specific email. Reveals domains owned by that email.

sections.title: GitHub OSINT — Developers Leak Everything
sections.description: GitHub is a goldmine for OSINT. Developers accidentally commit API keys, passwords, internal URLs, and email addresses. Even deleted code can be recovered from git history.
sections.note: Never use found credentials for unauthorized access. This technique is for understanding exposure and digital footprint only.

tools.name: TruffleHog
tools.description: Scans git history for high-entropy strings and known secret patterns (API keys, passwords).

tools.name: GitDorker
tools.description: Automated GitHub dorking tool. Searches for secrets and sensitive data across repositories.

commands.description: Search all GitHub commits for a specific email address.
Search a specific user's repositories for exposed API keys.
Search a user's code for hardcoded passwords.
Scan a GitHub repository's full history for leaked secrets and API keys.
GitHub API — get public profile: name, bio, location, company, followers, creation date.
List all public repositories of a GitHub user with full metadata.

sections.title: Telegram OSINT
sections.description: Telegram is widely used and often overlooked in OSINT. Public groups, channels, and usernames can reveal a lot about a target's activities, connections, and identity.
sections.note: Telegram shows phone numbers only to contacts. But username, bio, profile picture, and group memberships are often publicly visible.

tools.name: TGStat
tools.description: Telegram channel and group analytics. Search by keyword, find related channels, view growth stats.

tools.name: Telegago
tools.description: Google-powered Telegram search engine. Find public groups and channels by keyword.

commands.description: Direct link to a Telegram user or channel profile. View public bio and profile picture.
Google dork to find public Telegram groups and channels related to a keyword.
Search for a Telegram username across indexed pages.
Telegram Bot API — get public info about any channel or group. Requires a bot token.

sections.title: Phone Number OSINT
sections.description: A phone number can reveal carrier, country, region, and linked accounts. Many services use phone numbers as identifiers that can be cross-referenced across platforms.
sections.note: Phone number lookup results vary by country and carrier. Always verify findings independently.

tools.name: PhoneInfoga
tools.description: Advanced phone number OSINT tool. Scans multiple sources for carrier, location, and linked accounts.

tools.name: NumLookup
tools.description: Free phone number lookup. Returns carrier, line type, and country info.

commands.description: Download PhoneInfoga from GitHub.
Scan a phone number. Use international format with country code (e.g. +92 for Pakistan).
Launch PhoneInfoga web interface on localhost for easier use.
NumLookup API — get carrier, line type, country for a phone number.
Search for a phone number across major social platforms.

sections.title: DNS & Passive DNS OSINT
sections.description: DNS records reveal infrastructure, hosting history, and connected services. Passive DNS databases store historical DNS records — showing where a domain pointed in the past, even if changed.

commands.description: Get all DNS records for a domain: A, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME records.
Get TXT records — often contains SPF, DKIM, verification tokens that reveal services used.
Free DNS lookup API — returns all DNS records for a domain. No key needed.
Reverse IP lookup — find all domains hosted on the same IP address.
Find all subdomains of a domain using HackerTarget API. Free, no key needed.
SecurityTrails — view full DNS history. Shows past IP addresses and hosting changes.
